the rdfs:label -> Protein trap named in the spec; the label is uniprot:ACC, not a name

Do NOT turn this into a reviewed=1 filter - the previous note suggested it, and its premise was false.  UniprotConverter defaults `loadtrembl = true` and HumanMine's project.xml does not override it, so stock loads TrEMBL as well as Swiss-Prot.  Checked 2026-09-16: RDF Portal has 20,431 reviewed and 190,278 unreviewed human entries, and live HumanMine holds 117,219 human proteins - far more than Swiss-Prot alone.  A reviewed filter would drop ~83% of them.  There is no Protein field for the flag, so it is not loaded as data either.
Protein.sequence points at Sequence, which has no key attribute; the sub-node's own rows carry the data
isoform sequences - keep only the simple_sequence branch

spec D4, and DO NOT simply re-enable this.  obo:GO_0001618 -> GO:0001618 is right, but there is no correct single-hop target.  Protein's only OntologyTerm collection is `keywords` (filled by uniprot-keywords), and binding GOTerm.identifier here sent GO terms into it - visibly wrong in the emitted items.  InterMine models GO as Annotatable.ontologyAnnotations -> GOAnnotation -> ontologyTerm -> GOTerm, i.e. an intermediate object that `via` cannot express today (it is one Class.field).  Either teach items.py to synthesise the intermediate, or leave this to the existing go-annotation source, which already loads protein GO annotations with evidence codes.
keywords:NNN -> uniprot-keywords source stores identifier KW-NNNN; may need prefix:KW-
